Theme

Nature & food

foliage noun

also leaves (of a tree), leafy branch, greenery, in leaf

classical

Cic. Cael. 42: interclūsa jam frondibus et virgultīs (Lewis & Short)
Verg. G. 2.446: vīminibus salicēs fēcundī, frondibus ulmī (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 4.4.58 (Lewis & Short)

frōns, frondis f.

noun, third declension

leaves, foliage; a leafy bough

The leaves of a tree taken together, singular or plural; a single leaf is folium. Not to be confused with frōns, frontis, the forehead.

Examples

  • hīc ubi dēnsās agricolae stringunt frondēs

    here where the farmers are stripping the thick leavesVerg. E. 9.60–61

  • sed trūdit gemmās et frondēs explicat omnēs

    but it pushes out its buds and unfolds all its leavesVerg. G. 2.335

See also leaf, branch, tree, bud.

SourcesLewis & Short: frons

Vergil, Eclogae 9.60–61; Georgica 2.335.
